title: Phone Stand — Nine Design Decisions
description: Synthetic nine-step example: geometry, ghost pointer and reasoning are authored, not a recording of a real designer's session.

steps.title: Establish the footprint
steps.goal: Set a footprint that stays stable when the screen is tapped.

operation.instruction: Sketch a 100 × 80 mm rectangle on the XY plane and extrude it 7 mm.

reasoning.text: I choose a wide base first so I can evaluate stability before fixing the viewing angle. The depth matters more than the width: tapping the screen pushes the phone backwards.

cues.label: First, I define a broad footprint for stability.
Now I extrude it, keeping the plate relatively thin.
This dimension is a design choice, not a requirement.

decision.question: How deep should the base be?
criteria: Resists tipping when the screen is tapped

options.label: Compact
options.note: Small, but tips backwards when tapped.

options.label: Balanced
options.note: Stable for phones up to ~7 inch.

options.label: Generous
options.note: Very stable, takes more desk space.

scope.note: Depth sized for phones up to ~7 inch

steps.title: Choose a viewing angle
steps.goal: Hold the screen at a comfortable angle.

operation.instruction: Extrude a 6 mm back panel and tilt it 25° back from vertical (65° from the desk).

reasoning.text: The back panel is angled for viewing, but I keep the angle as one parameter so I can change its inclination if the phone or the context changes.

cues.label: I introduce a back panel to carry the phone.
I tilt it instead of assuming the first angle is final.
The angle depends on how the stand will be used.

decision.question: How steep should the phone lean?
criteria: Eye level while sitting at a desk

options.label: Shallow
options.note: Easy to tap, but the screen reflects ceiling lights.

options.label: Medium
options.note: Readable from a chair; still stable when tapped.

options.label: Upright
options.note: Good for video calls, tips more easily.

scope.note: Angle chosen for reading at a desk

steps.title: Prevent the phone from sliding
steps.goal: Stop the phone from sliding off the base.

operation.instruction: Sketch a 6 mm strip near the front edge and extrude it 10 mm up.

reasoning.text: I add a shallow lip to prevent slipping while leaving room to reach the bottom of the device. Higher than about a centimeter starts covering the screen.

cues.label: A small lip holds the device near the lower edge.
I extrude only enough to resist sliding.
The phone size might call for a different lip.

decision.question: How tall should the retaining lip be?
criteria: Holds the phone at the chosen angle

options.label: Low
options.note: Covers nothing, but a cased phone can slip over it.

options.label: Medium
options.note: Holds a cased phone without covering the screen.

options.label: High
options.note: Very secure, hides the bottom of the screen.

scope.note: Height assumes a phone in a case

steps.title: Round the base edges
steps.goal: Make the base pleasant to handle without losing contact area.

operation.instruction: Select the four vertical base edges and fillet them with an 8 mm radius.

reasoning.text: Before moving to details, I soften the sharp base corners for handling while keeping enough flat contact for stability. A large radius would eat into the footprint I chose in step 1.

cues.label: A wide base helps stability, but sharp corners feel unfinished.
I increase the fillet radius a little at a time.
Too much rounding would take away useful flat contact.

decision.question: How much should the base corners be rounded?

options.label: Break the edge
options.note: Just removes sharpness.

options.label: Soft
options.note: Friendly look, contact area barely changes.

options.label: Pebble
options.note: Very soft, but the footprint shrinks noticeably.

scope.note: Softening edges without losing contact area

steps.title: Leave a charging-cable passage
steps.goal: Allow charging while the phone is on the stand.

operation.instruction: Sketch a 20 mm wide slot centered on the lip and cut through it.

reasoning.text: The retaining lip should not block charging. I cut a centered cable passage but keep support on both sides, so the phone still cannot slide.

cues.label: The phone still needs to charge while it is on the stand.
I remove a small section of the front lip.
Both lip segments remain to prevent sliding.

decision.question: How wide should the cable passage be?
criteria: Keeps enough lip on both sides

options.label: Narrow
options.note: Fits a bare cable, not a USB-C plug housing.

options.label: Medium
options.note: Fits most plugs; both lip halves still hold.

options.label: Wide
options.note: Fits any plug, lip halves get short.

scope.note: Keep charging access whenever a lip is used

steps.title: Reinforce the back support
steps.goal: Keep the tilted back from flexing when the screen is tapped.

operation.instruction: Sketch a triangular rib on a side plane, extrude it 6 mm, mirror it across the YZ midplane.

reasoning.text: The angled back may flex. I add a pair of narrow ribs near the sides instead of filling the entire area with material, and mirror one rib so both sides stay identical when I edit it.

cues.label: The tilted back panel may need more stiffness.
I build a narrow triangular rib near one side.
I mirror the structural idea to keep the support balanced.

decision.question: How should the tilted back be stiffened?
criteria: Edits stay consistent on both sides

options.label: Thicker panel
options.note: Simple, but doubles the panel's material.

options.label: One central rib
options.note: Blocks the cable path behind the phone.

options.label: Two mirrored side ribs
options.note: Stiff, light, and one edit updates both.

scope.note: Stiffen a tilted panel locally instead of thickening it

steps.title: Pattern four anti-slip pads
steps.goal: Keep the stand from sliding on the desk.

operation.instruction: Extrude one 12 mm pad under a corner, then pattern it 2 × 2.

reasoning.text: Instead of making the base heavier, I use four small contact pads to increase friction and stabilize the stand on an uneven table. Patterning one pad means I edit all four at once.

cues.label: The stand should not slide on the desk.
I place grip pads near the base corners.
Four pads give support without extending the footprint.

decision.question: How should the stand resist sliding?

options.label: Heavier base
options.note: Works, but adds material and print time.

options.label: Full rubber sheet
options.note: Grippy, but rocks on uneven tables.

options.label: Four corner pads
options.note: Three-point-like contact, no rocking.

steps.title: Lighten the back support
steps.goal: Use less material without losing the side rails.

operation.instruction: Sketch a 60 × 45 mm window on the back panel and cut through it.

reasoning.text: A solid back panel uses more material than needed. I explore a central opening while retaining side rails, accepting that it may reduce stiffness — the ribs from step 6 make that acceptable.

cues.label: The solid back support may use unnecessary material.
I cut an opening through its center.
The side rails remain, but strength should still be checked.

decision.question: Should the back panel be lightened?

options.label: Keep it solid
options.note: Stiffest, most material.

options.label: Central window
options.note: Saves ~40% of the panel; ribs keep it stiff.

options.label: Slots
options.note: Looks technical, harder to print without supports.

scope.note: Acceptable only because of the ribs

steps.title: Check phone fit and clearance
steps.goal: Verify angle, lip and charging access with a real phone size.

operation.instruction: Insert a 75 × 150 × 8 mm phone proxy and move it against the back and lip.

reasoning.text: I bring in a simplified phone proxy to check the viewing angle, charging access, and whether the lip clears the device before committing to dimensions. The proxy is temporary and not printed.

cues.label: I want to check the design with a phone-sized object.
I position a temporary proxy against the angled back.
I inspect the lip and charging clearance before finalizing.

decision.question: How do you verify the stand fits the phone?

options.label: Trust the dimensions
options.note: Fast; mistakes show up only after printing.

options.label: Phone proxy in CAD
options.note: Cheap check of angle, lip and port access.

options.label: Print a test slice
options.note: Most reliable, costs a print.

scope.note: Check against a real device size before finalizing

brief.goal: A printable stand for reading and watching on a phone at a desk
brief.users: Office workers with 6–7 inch phones, often in a case
constraints: Stable when the screen is tapped
